note: The sky and its clouds (WLD-035, WLD-036). Drawn by Prototype/play/play.js; nothing here is stored or ticked: the clouds' place and shape are worked out from the world clock. Colours are linear RGB, 0 to 1. zenith is the blue overhead on a clear day (greener than it looks: the picture's tone curve turns a pure blue to purple) and brightness scales it; depth is how much of it replaces the hazy sky (0 keeps the pale haze of the reference renders, 1 is all blue overhead); the horizon always stays hazy (W5). sun_ref is the sun strength at which the blue is at full brightness. clouds.cover is the share of sky covered for each kind of weather; follow_weather false means the sky always uses cover.clear (the owner switched it on, 2026-11-22). scale sets the size of the clouds (bigger number, smaller clouds), soft the softness of their edges, wind the direction they drift, speed how far they drift per game minute, change how fast they change shape, lit and shade how bright their sunny and shaded sides are, blend_minutes how long the sky takes to change when the weather does. weather says what each kind of weather does to the light (WLD-037): sun is the share of direct sunlight that gets through, haze multiplies the thickness of the air, veil adds pale light to the sky and the distance, grey darkens the clouds, rain is how hard it rains (0 none, 1 steady). overcast_fill is how much of the sunlight the clouds stop comes down as soft grey light instead. rain sets the drops (alpha how visible, slant how far they lean, speed how fast they fall in metres a second, length how long their streaks are in metres), how much wet paving darkens (wet_dark) and shines towards the light (wet_sheen), how full the puddles get (puddles, 0 to 1), how strong the rings are where drops land (ripples), and how long it takes to dry after the rain stops (dry_minutes, at most one weather slot).
